references.text: Luke describes Jesus' daily teaching in the temple in a summarizing parallel: "During the day he was in the temple and taught" ([ref:Luk 21:37|Luke 21:37]).
The chief priests and the scribes sought a way to have Jesus killed, a direct continuation of the intention described in 19:47 ([ref:Luk 22:2|Luke 22:2]).
Mark's parallel account: "The chief priests and the scribes heard it and sought a way to get rid of him" ([ref:Mark 11:18|Mark 11:18]).
In Mark, the chief priests and the scribes plan to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him ([ref:Mark 14:1|Mark 14:1]).
Matthew tells of Jesus' teaching in the temple where the chief priests and the elders of the people confront him ([ref:Matt 21:23|Matthew 21:23]).
The chief priests and the elders of the people gathered to plan Jesus' arrest and execution ([ref:Matt 26:3-4|Matthew 26:3-4]).
Jesus asks why they seek to kill him, showing the ongoing murder plot against him ([ref:Joh 7:19|John 7:19]).
Jesus confronts them by saying that they seek to kill him: "you seek to kill me" ([ref:Joh 8:37|John 8:37]).
After the raising of Lazarus, they planned to kill Jesus, a parallel to the religious leaders' opposition ([ref:Joh 11:53|John 11:53]).
At his arrest, Jesus says that he always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, referring to his daily teaching ([ref:Joh 18:20|John 18:20]).

One of those days while he was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the gospel, the chief priests and the scribes with the elders came – an elaboration of the daily teaching mentioned in 19:47 ([ref:Luk 20:1|Luke 20:1]).
The scribes and the chief priests wanted to lay hands on him at that very moment, but they feared the people – the same pattern of murder plots hindered by the crowd ([ref:Luk 20:19|Luke 20:19]).
The psalmist prophesies that the nations and kings rise up against the Lord and his anointed – a messianic psalm anticipating the leaders' opposition to Christ ([ref:Sal 2:1-2|Psalms 2:1-2]).
Isaiah prophesies about the Lord's servant who is despised and rejected by the people, a prediction of the opposition Jesus faced from the leaders ([ref:Jes 49:7|Isaiah 49:7]).
